method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: PRINTED NAME: both plates letter this corridor 'AVE. G. OR WINNIE' down the roadway I measured and print 70' in it (sheet 55 casings native 1039.4/1249.5, sheet 61 casings 1052.0/1260.0, both ~210 native px = 69 ft). HUNDRED-BLOCK BREAK: the corridor carries the 600|700 transition on the cross streets on BOTH plates. Sheet 55 (29th and 30th St faces): west of the line the runs end 619 621 623 / 620 622 624, east of it they begin 701 703 705 707 709 711 | 713 715 717 719 721 723 and 702 704 706 708 710 712 | 714 716 718 720 722 724. Sheet 61 (30th and 31st St faces): west of the line 613 615 617 619 621 623, east of it 701 703 705 707 709 711 | 713 715 717 719 721 723 and 702 704 ... 724. The corridor's own frontage confirms the streets: 2901-2927 / 2902-2928 on sheet 55 (29th-30th) and 3001-3027 / 3002-3028 on sheet 61 (30th-31st). ONE AVENUE WEST is AVE. F. OR CHURCH (lettered on sheet 55 cand2, ~1005 px west), with the entire 600 block - 601 603 605 607 609 611 | 613 615 617 619 621 623 and 602-624, Moore & Goodman Lumber Yard, blocks 388/389 - lying between Church and the reported line; Church carries the 500|600 break, not 600|700. ONE AVENUE EAST is AVE. H. OR BALL (lettered on sheet 55 cand1 at native 2148 and on sheet 61 cand2 at 2161), with the 800 block (801-823 / 802-824, Gulf City Cotton Press) beyond it; Ball carries the 700|800 break. Neither alternative shows 600|700, so neither can be this line. SEAM: 30TH ST is sheet 55's south edge (its crops print '61' in the bottom margin) and sheet 61's north edge (its crops print '55' in the top margin), so the two plates letter the same frontage on it. NOTE ON THE PROPOSED CANDIDATES (none is an avenue): sheet 55's 1757 / 740 / 2774 and sheet 61's 1434 / 2470 / 398 all land inside block interiors. Sheet 55's 1757 falls between street numbers 715 and 717 with the 700-block run continuing unbroken across it (the real mid-block feature there is the 20-ft alley, drawn dashed and labelled 6" W. PIPE / printed 20', about 130 px west); sheet 61's 1434 falls between 705 and 707 in the same 700 block, and its 2470 between 807 and 809 in the 800 block. None carries an avenue name or a hundred-block change. CORROBORATION: b-a from Winnie is +12.8 px; the same offset read from Ave H (Ball) near the seam is +12.4 (sheet 55 2148.5, sheet 61 2160.9), so the control is consistent to ~0.4 px. The avenue-to-avenue span Winnie->Ball measures 1005.1 px on sheet 55 and 1004.7 on sheet 61 (= 330 ft: 260-ft block + 70-ft avenue), confirming both plates are at the same drafted scale here. Independent checks against existing controls: pair_55_56 reads sheet 55's Ave I (Sealy) at 3159, and Winnie + 2 avenue-spans gives 3153; pair_16_61 reads sheet 61's Ave F (Church) at 155, and Winnie - one span gives 151.
measurement_note: Native x = raster x of work/sheets/1912w/u<unit>.jpg (3327x3898), origin top-left. Value is the midpoint of the two block-face casing lines bounding the 70-ft Winnie roadway, measured in the block row ADJACENT TO THE 30th St SEAM (sheet 55 y 3100-3500, centres 1143.2-1143.5, at the seam y~3600: 1143.4; sheet 61 y 0-500, centres 1155.8-1156.7, at the seam y~200: 1156.2). Both plates are nearly square to the raster here (sheet 55 drifts only 1145 at top to 1143 at bottom over the full 3898 rows), so the reading is insensitive to the row chosen. Ruler-read values off the supplied crops (sheet_55_cand1 and cand2, sheet_61_cand1) reproduce these to 1.1 px.
